description: A message written while the agent is busy with a turn: not sent yet, it waits in the queue just under the conversation (above the composer), drawn as your bubble but grey. Hovering its row shows delete, send-now and edit buttons beside it.
opens: Enter in the composer (with text or attachments) while a turn runs

parts.name: bubble
parts.shows: Same shape and content as a sent message's bubble (attachments row, then markdown text), right-aligned, but filled with the text colour at 7% and its text at 55% opacity (grey), not the accent. Queued messages stack 10px apart, oldest first, below the last message of the chat and above the composer; the queue takes no room when empty.

parts.name: buttons
parts.shows: Three small round flat buttons (24px) in a row just left of the bubble, their middle level with the middle of its last line of text, invisible until the pointer is on the row, fading in over 150ms: ✕ (close icon), ↑ (a bold arrow character), and the circular-arrows revert icon. They stay beside the bubble whatever the message ends with (a list, a numbered list, a code block).

decisions.said: A bullet or numbered list on a message's last line pushes the Send now / Revert buttons well out of place
decisions.rule: Every app keeps a message's buttons just beside its bubble, level with its last line, whatever the message ends with (a list, a numbered list, a code block): what's inside a bubble never widens the bubble's share of the row

decisions.said: On mobile a single click of a user message should reveal the revert, send now .etc buttons
decisions.rule: Every app shows a message's buttons without hover where there is none: on a touch screen a single tap on the message shows them (a long press too) and another tap hides them; with a pointer, hovering its row shows them

decisions.said: Said buttons must be center aligned with the text on the last line of the message it is not so at the moment
decisions.rule: Every app centres a message's buttons on the middle of the bubble's last line of text, at any text size

phone.does: A tap on the message shows the same buttons, centred on its last line of text as here; another tap hides them. A long press shows them too
phone.why: No hover on touch; the owner asked for a single tap

actions.does: Drops it from the queue. Tooltip "Delete this queued message".

Interrupts the running turn, then sends this message and every queued message before it, together as one message (their texts joined by a blank line, their attachments together). Tooltip "Send now: interrupt the chat, then send this and the queued messages before it".

Takes it out of the queue and puts its text in the composer before what's already written there (separated by a blank line), caret after its text, its attachments back in the composer's strip. Tooltip "Edit: put this message back in the box".

states.name: turn ends by itself
states.shows: Every queued message is sent at once, together as one message (texts joined by blank lines); they leave the queue and the sent message appears in the chat as a normal sent bubble.

states.name: turn stopped (Esc / stop button)

decisions.said: You can get into a state where messages are queued, but the agent is not currently owrking / it is interrupted. Once interrupted, queued messsges should automatically be sent into te model.
decisions.rule: Every app sends the queue when a turn ends, whether it ended by itself or was interrupted

states.shows: Once the stopped turn ends, the queue is sent as when a turn ends by itself (all of it as one message, or up to the one whose ↑ was pressed).

states.name: another chat opened
states.shows: The queue stays with the chat it was written in, kept beside that chat's draft (on disk on the phone, over a restart on the desktop), and is drawn under its conversation again, as it was, when the chat is opened again. A new chat's queue goes into its box instead.

decisions.said: Going to another chat and back un-queues a queued message; queued messages should persist across chats (paraphrased)
decisions.rule: Every app keeps a chat's queued messages with that chat when another is opened, draws them again when it's opened, and sends them to it when its turn ends meanwhile

states.name: turn ends while another chat is open
states.shows: The left chat's queue is sent to it as its turn ends, by itself or stopped, as if it were open: all of it as one message, or up to the one whose ↑ stopped the turn. The sent message is in that chat's conversation when it is opened. Only a turn's end the app sees sends it; one sent whose host may not have taken it goes back to the front of the queue and is sent again by the same uuid, which its host takes once.

states.name: in history
states.shows: A message Claude Code recorded as sent mid-turn (queued_command) is drawn in a reopened chat as an ordinary sent message (UserTurn).
